# Overturning Citizens United, Movement Voter Project's numbers, and four Epstein-records links

Checked: November 19, 2026. Verdict key: CONFIRMED / DISAGREE / NOT USED.

Origin: a research file on work to overturn *Citizens United* supplied by the site owner, four screenshots (one OpenSecrets page and three Movement Voter Project FAQ pages), and four links about the Epstein files. Every figure below was re-read at the cited page, not taken from the file or the screenshots. Web-search summaries were used only to find pages. Pages behind a bot check (GovTrack, congress.gov) were not opened; official data from govinfo.gov was used instead.

## Overturning Citizens United

- **How it can be overturned.** CONFIRMED. The ruling interpreted the First Amendment, so ordinary legislation cannot undo it. Article V: Congress proposes an amendment when two-thirds of both houses agree (or Congress calls a convention when two-thirds of state legislatures apply), and it takes effect when three-fourths of the states ratify, which is 38. https://www.archives.gov/founding-docs/constitution-transcript
- **Five amendments are pending in the 119th Congress.** CONFIRMED against the introduced text and the bill-status record at govinfo.gov (status files updated Sept. 22 to Nov. 18, 2026). The file listed four; a fifth exists.
  - **H.J.Res. 54** (Rep. Pramila Jayapal, D-WA), introduced Feb. 12, 2025. Rights belong to "natural persons only"; entities have no constitutional rights; governments "shall regulate, limit, or prohibit" contributions and expenditures; courts may not treat election spending as First Amendment speech; press protected. 82 cosponsors, all Democrats. Move to Amend's site tracks its cosponsors.
  - **H.J.Res. 119** (Rep. Jim McGovern, D-MA), introduced Sept. 10, 2025. Eight sections. No person may spend or contribute more than $100 a year to influence another person's election, nor more than $1,000 in aggregate; no corporation may spend or contribute to influence federal elections; Congress must enact limits and public funding of at least 80% of allowed spending within 60 days or members' pay is suspended; states may set their own limits. 0 cosponsors.
  - **H.J.Res. 121** (Rep. Mary Gay Scanlon, D-PA), introduced Sept. 11, 2025. Congress and the states "may regulate and set reasonable limits" on money to influence elections and may distinguish natural persons from corporations, including banning corporate election spending. Needs implementing laws. 48 cosponsors, all Democrats. Senate companion **S.J.Res. 43** (Sen. Jeanne Shaheen, D-NH), introduced March 27, 2025: 41 cosponsors (39 Democrats, 2 independents).
  - **H.J.Res. 122** (Rep. Joe Neguse, D-CO), introduced Sept. 17, 2025. Like 121 but requires limits to be "viewpoint-neutral," expressly allows public-financing systems, and sets a seven-year ratification deadline. 114 cosponsors, all Democrats.
  - **H.J.Res. 191** (Rep. Tom Barrett, R-MI), introduced June 3, 2026. Congress and the States may reasonably regulate and limit contributions and spending in campaigns and in state or local ballot measures, including by distinguishing natural persons from artificial entities. Seven-year deadline. One cosponsor, Rep. Ro Khanna (D-CA), added July 2, 2026. American Promise issued a statement on it June 4.
  - All referred to the House or Senate Judiciary Committee; the status record shows no later action. Sources: https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/BILLS-119hjres54ih/html/BILLS-119hjres54ih.htm and the same address with hjres119, hjres121, hjres122 and hjres191 (ih = introduced text); status files at https://www.govinfo.gov/bulkdata/BILLSTATUS/119/hjres/BILLSTATUS-119hjres121.xml (and the other numbers; sjres/BILLSTATUS-119sjres43.xml).
- **DISAGREE with the file on H.J.Res. 119.** The file says it "caps individual federal donations at $100." The text says $100 a year to influence *another person's* election and a separate $1,000 aggregate cap including a person's own spending and gifts to candidates, campaigns and parties. Also, the file says it has "Sections 5-7"; it has eight.
- **NOT USED: "Sen. Adam Schiff co-led H.J.Res. 122."** A senator cannot cosponsor a House resolution, and no Senate companion by Schiff was found. The file also names Sen. Alex Padilla and Rep. Daniel Goldman as notable cosponsors of H.J.Res. 121; Goldman appears on 122, and we did not check Padilla. Not repeated.
- **How many states have called for an amendment.** DISAGREE with the file's "22 states." American Promise's home page (read Nov. 19) says 25 states and counting; Move to Amend's home page says 25 states taking action. The Brennan Center counted 23 in January 2026 (already on the Money page). The count depends on who counts and when.
- **Local resolutions.** DISAGREE with "nearly 800." Move to Amend's home page says 700+ local resolutions and 820+ endorsing organizations; that is the group's own count. American Promise's local count was not found.
- **Groups differ on which amendment to back.** CONFIRMED. Move to Amend (Nov. 17, 2026) argues that an amendment dealing only with election spending could leave corporations with constitutional claims against public-interest laws, and urges language that also ends corporate constitutional rights. The narrower amendments' sponsors and American Promise describe theirs as restoring lawmakers' authority to set limits. Both are arguments by advocacy groups.
- **Groups.** CONFIRMED at each group's own pages and IRS/FEC records:
  - American Promise Inc (501(c)(4), EIN 47-4608840) and American Promise Education Fund Inc (501(c)(3), EIN 47-4601462), Concord, MA; ProPublica. Says it is uniting Americans behind the For Our Freedom Amendment; describes its work as cross-partisan.
  - Free Speech For People Inc (501(c)(3), EIN 45-0709993). Its site calls it a national non-profit non-partisan organization founded in January 2010 on the day of the ruling, and says donations are tax-deductible. Its current campaigns also include impeachment and immigration enforcement.
  - Move to Amend (501(c)(4), EIN 46-4306740, Sacramento, CA).
  - End Citizens United: federal PAC (FEC C00573261, active), ECU Action Fund (FEC C90023607), and End Citizens United-Let America Vote Action Fund (501(c)(4), EIN 82-4671419). Its 2026 endorsements page lists candidates including Ossoff, Peltola, Acton, Klobuchar, Hinojosa, Benson and Sand; the file's claim that ECU endorsed Benson, Sand, Acton and Klobuchar is CONFIRMED. We did not check whether Benson or Sand won; not stated.
  - Public Citizen Inc (501(c)(4), EIN 23-7104508) and Public Citizen Foundation (501(c)(3), EIN 52-1263996). Its About page says that with rare exceptions it does not participate in partisan political activities or endorse candidates, and takes no government or corporate money.
- **NOT USED from the file:** the list of law firms said to give pro bono help; the profiles of named scholars and activists; statements about Govs. Newsom and Polis, Seattle's democracy vouchers as mayoral advocacy, and "hundreds of mayors" signing proclamations; Sanders' amendments "since 2011"; "Common Cause chapters in 35 states." Not checked at a source, or not needed. U.S. PIRG, Demos and Equal Citizens were not added to the directory.

## Movement Voter Project (MVP)

- **OpenSecrets page.** CONFIRMED, live page read Nov. 19, 2026 (the screenshot showed an earlier version: rank 91 of 40,499; the live page says 51 of 40,455). 2024 cycle contributions $19,121,027, including affiliate Movement Voter PAC; lobbying $0; outside spending $0. The recipient breakdown shows $14,727,440 (99.85%) to outside groups and $14,626 (0.10%) to candidates. Top recipients: Victory PAC (Arizona) $1,505,000; Workers Vote $1,340,000; Casa in Action PAC $1,170,000. OpenSecrets' own totals and breakdown do not add up exactly ($19.1 million versus about $14.7 million in sources); we use the headline total and the shares as OpenSecrets states them. FEC totals were released Feb. 6, 2025. https://www.opensecrets.org/orgs/movement-voter-project/summary?id=D000073515
- **MVP's own money count.** CONFIRMED as MVP's claim (page "Updated October 14, 2026"): more than $184 million in "partisan funds" since 2016, $82+ million in 2023-2024 and $29 million in 2025-2026 to date. The page says the figures include money moved by Movement Voter PAC and its 501(c)(4) sibling through grants, "as well as gifts MVP advised its donors to make directly to grantees." The gap with OpenSecrets is large and the two count different things; we did not reconcile them. https://movement.vote/faq/how-much-partisan-money-has-mvp-moved/
- **MVP's impact claims.** CONFIRMED as MVP's claims, not as facts. 2024: partners reached "over one million" likely Democratic voters not contacted by other programs, helped protect four Senate seats and flip at least seven House seats, reduced Harris's loss margins in three states. A Nov. 21, 2025 MVP analysis estimates 220,635 net votes. 2025: claims of roles in Virginia, New Jersey, California's Prop 50, state supreme court races and two Georgia Public Service Commission races. We found no independent evaluation of these figures. https://movement.vote/faq/what-was-mvps-impact-on-the-2024-elections/ , https://movement.vote/faq/what-was-mvps-impact-on-the-2025-elections/ , https://movement.vote/blog/2025-11-21-new-analysis-evidence-of-electoral-impact-in-2024/
- **Screenshots.** Not reproduced on the site: they are third-party page images (and the OpenSecrets one is out of date). The facts are summarized in text with links and dates.

## Epstein records links

- **DOJ Epstein Library and search.** CONFIRMED, official. justice.gov/epstein ("Last Updated: September 11, 2026") and justice.gov/epstein/search. Age gate; warns that the library may include sexual content and non-public personal information despite redactions; says some materials are not reliably searchable. https://www.justice.gov/epstein
- **Epstein Files Transparency Act (H.R. 4405).** CONFIRMED. govinfo bill status: became Public Law 119-38 on Nov. 19, 2025.
- **SDSU library guide.** CONFIRMED. A San Diego State University library research guide (librarian Kate Holvoet) with background, best practices and lists of official and public search platforms. Library guide, not an official source. https://libguides.sdsu.edu/epsteinfiles
- **epsteinlibrary.com.** CONFIRMED to exist and to say it searches documents released under H.R. 4405. Operator not identified on the page (a contact email and a Ko-fi donation link); shows a content warning and support-hotline list. Not affiliated with the government as far as the page shows. Completeness not checked.
- **epstein-stats.vercel.app.** CONFIRMED to exist. Says it indexes 1.4 million-plus documents from DOJ, SDNY, House Oversight and the FBI Vault; "Index last updated: Jun 1, 2026"; says it is not affiliated with the U.S. Government and that appearance of a name does not imply guilt or wrongdoing. Operator not identified. It labels named individuals by legal classification; we did not check any of those labels.
- The two unofficial tools are listed with those limits. The site makes no claims about any person named in the records.
